desc: Each of the six reports returns rows in a normal range
control: Control: the same call shape returns 0 for QB Location, so a non-zero here is real.

desc: The account reaches more than one location
control: Control: the endpoint returns a list; a single-location account would return 1.

desc: At least TWO locations each carry invoices in the same range
control: Control: the identical call for QB Location returns 0 rows, so these counts discriminate.

desc: Three or more customers with invoices
control: Control: distinct names counted from rows actually read (245 read).

desc: A customer whose invoices span TWO locations
control: Control: the same query with ONE location returns zero "Multiple" rows.

desc: A row whose Subtotal is zero or below (em-dash Margin %)
control: Control: 245 rows read and 233 had subtotal > 0, so the filter discriminates.

desc: Rows with NEGATIVE Inv. Hrs
control: Control: both signs counted; finding both proves the field is being read.

desc: Enough customers to span more than one page (>30)
control: Control: rowsNumber comes from the server pagination block, not from len(rows).

desc: A customer with two or more invoices
control: Control: invoice_count read per row; 92 of 245 had exactly 1, so it discriminates.

desc: Two or more sales representatives on the report
control: Control: single-location call returns 3; two-location call should be >= that.

desc: An INACTIVE sales representative with invoices
control: Control: both flags counted; finding both values proves the field is populated.

desc: An UNASSIGNED invoice row (Show Unassigned)
control: Control: the flag is toggled BOTH ways; if the counts are identical the parameter is being ignored and the result is NOT evidence either way.

desc: A rep with invoices at TWO locations, and one at a single location
control: Control: run over ALL SIX locations, not a chosen pair. The two-location subset returned 0 and that reading was WRONG -- recorded in PRECONDITIONS.md.

desc: Parts with sales activity in the window
control: Control: the SAME query ascending returns 250 rows of demand 0, descending returns 250 of demand 8..700 -- so the probe demonstrably discriminates.

desc: BOTH inventory and Special Order rows present
control: Control: each type queried explicitly AND the two sum to the "both" total, which is what rules out a silently-ignored type parameter.

desc: Parts with Min and Max set
control: Control: counted as "not None"; if every row were None the count would be 0.

desc: Parts with different categories and different vendors
control: Control: both counted from rows read; 1 would mean uniform data, 0 a broken read.

desc: A part with NO category, one with NO vendor

evidence.note: no NULL category exists; the build uses a category literally named "Uncategorized" instead. Whether that satisfies "a part with NO category assigned" is the tester's reading, not ours.

control: Control: sorted by category in BOTH directions so a null at either end would be seen; the vendor half of the same rows DOES find nulls, which proves the "not set" test works and the category result is a real fact about the data.

desc: The same part number stocked at TWO locations
control: Control: BOTH sides read non-zero part sets, so an empty intersection would be a real fact about stocking, not an empty read. NOTE: only the first 250 rows of 5814/3620 are compared, so a zero here is NOT conclusive -- see the verdict text.

desc: A technician who clocked time and one who clocked NONE in the range
control: Control: the filter endpoint offers the same 39 as the wide report, so the report is not silently dropping anyone; the 2-day window is what creates the zero-time side, and it is a range the tester picks.

desc: A technician with internal hours but ZERO work-order hours
control: Control: rows with wo_seconds>0 are the complement and are numerous, so the field is populated and a match is a real find.

desc: A technician whose WO% lands on a ROUNDING TIE (x.x5)
control: Control: the percentage is recomputed from the raw seconds the API returns, so this is arithmetic on real data, not a guess. A tie is rare by nature -- ABSENT here means "not currently present", and it is seedable by clocking a chosen number of seconds.

desc: Technicians at two locations (for the multi-zone / per-location checks)
control: Control: two locations were explicitly selected; if only one appears that is a fact about where technicians clocked, not about the filter.

desc: The nightly capture has run for today (as_of date present)
control: Control: as_of_date is returned by the server in the response envelope.

desc: Inventory rows at two locations
control: Control: sorted by total_cost, so the first page may be single-location by chance; the per-location counts in F3/API-FACTS are the authoritative answer.

desc: All FOUR Work In Progress tabs contain rows
control: Control: each tab is fetched separately AND the server tab_counts block is read; the two agreeing is what rules out a mis-set tab parameter.

desc: Work orders with a non-zero money value, and a zero one
control: Control: three disjoint buckets counted over the same rows; they sum sensibly, so the field is being read.

desc: Work orders for two or more different ADVISORS
control: Control: counted from rows read; 1 would mean uniform data, 0 a broken read.

desc: Assets WITH a VIN and assets with NEITHER VIN nor Unit #
control: Control: all four tabs aggregated so the sample is the whole report, not one tab. The three buckets are disjoint and sum to rows.

desc: Work orders at two different locations
control: Control: per-location tab_counts (API-FACTS) show 136 and 59 estimates respectively, so both sides have data and a single value here would be a filter fault.

desc: Work orders in several STATUSES
control: Control: aggregated across all four tabs, which is where different statuses live.

desc: A filter combination exceeding 10,000 rows (the export cap)

evidence.note: SBC/SBR/WIP counts are far smaller; the cap is reachable on PV/IV only

control: Control: rowsNumber is the server total, independent of rowsPerPage.

desc: BOTH service (S) and parts (P) invoice numbers exist

evidence.why_not_absent: an unknown fraction of an unknown total, with the part-sale path unverified; a P-prefixed invoice may well exist

control: NO VALID CONTROL WAS ESTABLISHED for the P half. The S half is proven present. The correct next step is to capture the request the SBC expansion actually makes in the browser, rather than guessing a filter.

desc: A work order with NO vehicle (counter / parts sale)
control: Control: the complement (with a VIN) is counted in the same pass and is non-zero, so the fields are populated and a match is real.

desc: An invoice number longer than 18 characters, and one of exactly 18

evidence.caveat: the same 100-row server cap as F33 applies; the histogram shows a 7-11 character scheme, so >18 looks structurally impossible rather than merely unsampled -- but it is 100 rows of an unknown total

control: Control: a full length histogram is printed, so the zero is visibly a fact about the numbering scheme and not a failed read. Graded ABSENT_IN_SAMPLE, not ABSENT.

desc: Customer names with mixed upper/lower-case first letters
control: Control: both cases counted over the same rows; the uppercase side is large, so a zero lowercase count is a real fact about the names.

desc: A technician CURRENTLY CLOCKED IN on a line
control: Control: the field is an integer present on every row; rows with 0 are the majority, so a non-zero is a real live clock-in. This is time-of-day dependent.

desc: Work orders in Invoiced and in Paid status
control: Control: the full status histogram is printed, so a missing status is visible as such rather than inferred from a filtered query.
